question: Which native contract should retain authorship and reversible edits without requiring a particular review UI?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest stop verdict, at queue position 8. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One causal mutation model for accepted and proposed content, including dependencies, rebasing, collaboration admission and atomic review decisions.
Retained accepted history and selective compensation without invented or corrupted attribution.
Actorless reading and rendering of authored state; every authored write requires a non-empty author ID and the application owns authentication.
Editors that do not install the authored capability carry no identity requirement; review UI stays a Plate product choice.
Opening a saved document reads the current checkpoint directly, never by replaying the retained log.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 09-10 research, 09-12 scalability and loadable-state reviews, the 09-13 direct-checkpoint benchmark and the 09-16 identity analysis, plus today's suggestions and diff audit records. Rechecked on the live tree: AuthoredOptions, the write-time identity check and its error text, the authored package exports, DefaultAuthoredPlugin and its dependents in SuggestionPlugin and AIChatPlugin, and proposeAuthoredComparison's erased signature and message matching. No tests, browser, collaboration or benchmark were run.
summary: The job is to keep authorship, dependencies, retained content and selective reversal in one causal graph that any review UI can read, without inventing attribution. Live authored({ authorId, retainHistory }) accepts a fixed ID or a resolver. currentAuthorId is read once per write transaction, reads stay actorless, and a write with no identity throws 'An author ID is required for authored writes.', the accurate wording the 09-16 review asked for. Every alternative still loses. Identity only in proposing mode drops causal facts from accepted edits that rebase pending work. A Plite-generated anonymous author fabricates attribution. Bypassing capture for accepted edits creates a second mutation authority. A Yjs-attribution or document-mark replacement would not own retained content, atomic decisions or projected views. Two live defects sit next to this contract. DefaultAuthoredPlugin resolves Reflect.get(editor.runtime, 'userId') and SuggestionPlugin and AIChatPlugin hard-depend on it, and proposeAuthoredComparison in plitejs/authored takes AnyEditor and matches the identity error by message string. The suggestions and diff audits recorded today already pursue both, and neither target changes the native identity rule.

reconciliation.question: Should Plite allow ordinary accepted edits without an author ID when the authored capability is installed?
reconciliation.reason: Its Stop still holds on the live tree. Identity is required at the first authored write, reads stay actorless, and the error wording it flagged is now accurate.

alternatives: Keeping one authored path with write-time identity is selected. It is the only shape that keeps accepted edits in the causal graph without fabricating authors.

Requiring identity only for proposals and letting accepted edits bypass authored capture is rejected. Accepted edits rebase pending work and feed retained history, so bypass creates a second mutation authority.
Generating an anonymous or system author in Plite is rejected. It fabricates domain attribution and weakens same-author rules.

Replacing the native engine with Yjs attribution or ProseMirror-style suggestion marks is rejected. Neither owns retained content, atomic decisions, named roots or accepted versus proposed views, and today's suggestions audit found no evidence to reopen native ownership.

Folding the Plate identity bridge and the comparison import into this scope as a new Pursue is rejected as duplicate queue work. The suggestions audit owns one typed session actor, and the diff audit owns moving import onto the typed authored update owner.
proofLimits: Source review only; no authored, Yjs, browser or benchmark runs. The checkpoint performance receipt is historical. The decision page describes a version 4 checkpoint, which predates the clipboard plan's authored v5 change; the current version mapping was not rechecked, and any fix is a page refresh, not a new design. packages/plitejs/src/authored/checkpoint.ts and format.ts carry another session's uncommitted edits; no cited fact depends on them. This verdict assumes the suggestions and diff Pursues keep their recorded targets; if either is dropped, its gap returns to this scope.
